newsitem.title: USA: Washington Mutual Q1 profit a record.
newsitem.headline: Washington Mutual Q1 profit a record.

text.p: Washington Mutual Inc said Tuesday its first-quarter profit of $114.07 million was a record high and reflected in part the integration of American Savings Bank, which produced results exceeding expectations.
Washington Mutual said American Savings had loan originations of $1.5 billion in the quarter, compared to $1.3 billion a year ago. Washington Mutual acquired American Savings in late 1996.
Washington Mutual Chief Executive Kerry Killinger said the loan originations at American Savings reflected successful execution of a strategy to retain more loans.

Washington Mutual said aggressive marketing of checking accounts contributed to growth of more than 76,000 in households served between January 1 and the end of February, to 1.5 million, including 24,000 non-acquisition-related hoseholds.

Washington Mutual said net interest income rose to $317.0 million in the first quarter from $287.0 million a year ago, reflecting growth in the loan portfolio and an increase in the net interest spread to 2.77 percent from 2.75 percent.

Killinger, who is also chairman and president, said the company's strategy to manage interest rate risk should limit the effect of recent rate increases. He said the percentage of fixed-rate assets in the loan and mortgage-backed securities portfolio has been reduced in recent years.
Washington Mutual said it is anticipated that special meetings of shareholders of Washington Mutual and Great Western Financial Corp to approve a merger will be held in June.
H.F. Ahmanson and Co, a rival suitor for Great Western, has been pushing for a meeting in May.
